extracted.intended_audience: shippers, carriers, package designers, and compliance officers handling Class 7 (radioactive) materials; regulated entities and agency staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and compliance standards for packaging, labeling, marking, shipping paper descriptions, scope, definitions, and interagency coordination relating to transportation of Class 7 (radioactive) materials under the HMR (49 CFR parts 171-173).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination (RSPA/DOT with NRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: This rulemaking is being coordinated by RSPA with NRC to ensure that consistent regulatory standards are maintained for radioactive material transportation regulations, and to ensure coordinated publication of rules by both agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate rule text and publication timing with NRC to maintain consistency across agencies; work with DOT to ensure consistency with respect to the transportation of radioactive materials; conduct inspections of licensees in accordance with DOT requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act / small business accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must establish exceptions or differing compliance standards for small businesses where possible without undermining statutory objectives; in this rulemaking exceptions/differing standards were not possible, but an extended transition was provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule permits continued use of currently authorized DOT specification packagings for a period of 4 years following the final rule's effective date (effectively 5 years from publication) to minimize expected compliance costs for small businesses; certification that although the rule applies to a substantial number of small entities, there will not be a significant economic impact on those entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Executive Order 13272 and DOT procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule developed in accordance with Executive Order 13272 ('Proper Consideration of Small Entities in Agency Rulemaking') and DOT procedures to promote Regulatory Flexibility Act compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure potential impacts on small entities are properly considered during rulemaking and use applicable DOT processes for outreach/consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act: information collection approval
rubrics_metrics.description: RSPA has OMB information collection approval under OMB No. 2137-0510 (Radioactive (RAM) Transportation Requirements) with stated burden hours and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved collection: OMB No. 2137-0510; Number of Respondents: 3,817; Total Annual Responses: 21,519; Total Annual Burden Hours: 15,270; Total Annual Burden Cost: $139,895.60. Requests for copy directed to Deborah Boothe, DHM-10, RSPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation Identifier Number (RIN) cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A RIN is assigned to each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda; use the RIN in the document heading to cross-reference with the Unified Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unified Agenda published April and October; use RIN for cross-referencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule does not impose unfunded mandates under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 and does not result in costs of $100 million or more to governments or the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule determined to be the least burdensome alternative that achieves the objective of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Assessment finding
rubrics_metrics.description: NRC prepared an Environmental Assessment (EA) for major revision to packaging and transportation of radioactive material regulations which found no significant environmental impacts associated with this final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EA titled 'Environmental Assessment (EA) of Major Revision to Packaging and Transportation of Radioactive Material Regulations', Final Report, March 2002; EA available in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act / docket searchability
rubrics_metrics.description: Written communications and comments in dockets can be searched electronically by name of the submitting individual or signatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to DOT Privacy Act Statement (Federal Register, April 11, 2000) or visit http://dms.dot.gov for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials incorporated by reference (§171.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Update of referenced materials incorporated by reference, including addition/removal/revision of IAEA and ISO publications and addition of USEC material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Add 'IAEA, Regulations for the Safe Transport of Radioactive Material, 1996 Edition (Revised), No. TS-R-1'; add ISO 1496-1:1990 and ISO 9978:1992; add 'USEC-651—Good Handling Practices for Uranium Hexafluoride, Revision 8, January 1999.' Cross-reference applicable regulatory sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ICAO Technical Instructions (§171.11) — applicability to radioactive excepted packages
rubrics_metrics.description: ICAO Technical Instructions provisions apply except for excepted packages of Class 7 materials; specified subchapter provisions apply to Class 7 shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for excepted packages of Class 7 (radioactive) materials, the provisions of §§172.204(c)(4), 173.448(e),(f) and (g)(3) apply; excepted packages must meet provisions of §§173.421, 173.424, 173.426 or 173.428 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IAEA regulations for import/export (§171.12(d)) — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Class 7 materials imported into/exported from/passing through U.S. may be offered/accepted when prepared in accordance with IAEA TS-R-1 1996 edition if specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) highway route controlled quantities shipped per §§172.203(d)(4), 172.507 and 173.22(c); (2) competent authority certification and revalidation for fissile and Type B packages per §§173.471-173.473; (3) Type A package contents limited per §173.431; (4) country of origin has adopted TS-R-1 1996; (5) requirements of §173.448 fulfilled when applicable; (6) shipments comply with emergency response info in subpart G of part 172.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazardous Materials Table entries for Class 7 (§172.101 amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and revised Hazardous Materials Table entries specifying proper shipping names, hazard class, UN IDs, packing groups, label codes, special provisions, packaging references, quantity limits and carriage/exception details for various Class 7 descriptions (e.g., excepted package—articles, empty packagings, instruments; LSA-I/II/III; SCO; Type A/B packages; uranium hexafluoride).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table rows provide mapping between shipping description and applicable sections (e.g., UN2909, UN2912, UN3321, UN3322, UN2913, UN3327, UN2915, UN3332, UN3328, UN2916, UN2978, etc.), label codes, special provisions (A56,T5,TP4,W7), and references to §§173.xxx for packaging and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional shipping paper description requirements for Class 7 (§172.203(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Shipping paper descriptions for a shipment of Class 7 material must include specific additional entries as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required entries: (1) name of each radionuclide listed in §173.435 (or per §173.433(f) for mixtures; abbreviations authorized); (2) physical and chemical form if not special form (generic chemical description acceptable); (3) activity in each package in appropriate SI units (customary units may follow in parentheses); (4) category of label applied (e.g., 'RADIOACTIVE WHITE-I'); (5) transport index assigned for packages bearing YELLOW-II or YELLOW-III; (6) for fissile packages: (i) 'Fissile Excepted' if excepted per §173.453 or (ii) criticality safety index; (7) notation of DOE or NRC package identification marking for approved packages (see §173.471); (8) notation of IAEA Certificate of Competent Authority package identification for export/foreign-made packages (see §173.473); (9) indication if consigned as exclusive use or single 'Exclusive Use Shipment' statement; (10) for highway route controlled quantity packages the words 'Highway route controlled quantity' or 'HRCQ' associated with the basic description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirements for Class 7 packages (§172.310)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to other required markings, specific markings must appear on packages containing Class 7 materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (a) packages >50 kg gross mass must be marked with gross mass including unit; (b) industrial, Type A, Type B(U), Type B(M) packages must be legibly/durably marked with 'TYPE IP-1', 'TYPE IP-2', 'TYPE IP-3', 'TYPE A', 'TYPE B(U)' or 'TYPE B(M)' in letters at least 13 mm high; (c) IP-1/2/3 or Type A packages must be marked with international vehicle registration code of country of origin (USA for US designs); (d) Type B(U)/B(M) outermost receptacle must be plainly marked with a radiation symbol conforming to Appendix B and be resistant to fire/water; (e) Type B(U), Type B(M) or fissile packages destined for export must also be marked 'USA' with the specification marking or package certificate identification (see §§173.471-173.473).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of FISSILE label to labeling requirements (§172.400/§172.441)
rubrics_metrics.description: A FISSILE label is added for fissile radioactive material (see §172.441), with the label design referenced in §172.441 and specific background color requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hazard class/division table updated to include 'FISSILE' label for 7 (fissile radioactive material; see §172.402) with design reference 172.441. §172.441 requires background color white in addition to compliance with §172.407; otherwise label as specified (size/color excepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional labeling requirements for Class 7 packages (§172.402)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each package containing Class 7 material that also meets additional hazard class definitions must be labeled as a Class 7 material and for each additional hazard, subject to certain exceptions; special requirements for fissile material labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) A subsidiary label is not required on the package if the material conforms to the remaining criteria in §173.4; (2) Each package or overpack containing fissile material, other than fissile-excepted material, must bear two FISSILE labels affixed to opposite sides, conforming to the figure in §172.441 and affixed adjacent to radioactive material labels where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class 7 label contents and overpack labeling rules (§172.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed content requirements for Class 7 labels and rules for labeling overpacks/freight containers containing Class 7 packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FISSILE label: must be completed with criticality safety index (CSI) assigned in NRC/DOE package design approval or competent authority certificate; for overpacks/freight containers CSI is sum of CSIs for packages contained. For Class 7 labels generally: (g)(1) Contents: names of radionuclides per §173.435 (LSA-I may use 'LSA-I'); (g)(2) Activity: expressed in SI units (customary units may follow in parentheses); (g)(3) Transport index per §173.403. Overpack rules (§172.403(h)): (1) contents may state 'mixed' if inside packages differ; (2) activity = sum of becquerels of contained packages; (3) transport index = sum of TIs of contained packages or, for rigid overpack, may be direct measured per §173.403; (4) category of Class 7 label for overpack determined from table in §172.403(c) using derived TI and maximum surface radiation level; (5) overpack label category used (not constituent package categories) to determine vehicle placarding per Table 1 of §172.504(e); (6) for fissile material, overpack CSI = sum of individual package CSIs as stated in certificate of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISSILE label completion with CSI (§172.403(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: FISSILE labels for packages required to bear them must be completed with the criticality safety index (CSI) assigned in the NRC or DOE package design approval or competent authority certificate; overpack/freight container CSI must be the sum of contained package CSIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For overpacks and freight containers required to bear a FISSILE label, use arithmetic sum of CSIs of all packages contained in the overpack/freight container.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISSILE label appearance requirement (§172.441)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to complying with §172.407, the background color on the FISSILE label must be white; otherwise label appearance follows §172.441 specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label must conform to size and color specifications in §172.441 (white background) and comply with §172.407 general label requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exceptions to Part 173 (§173.401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain materials/conditions are excluded from the scope of Part 173.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include: (b)(2) Class 7 materials implanted or incorporated into and still in a person or live animal for diagnosis/treatment; (b)(3) Class 7 material that is an integral part of the means of transport; (b)(4) natural material and ores containing naturally occurring radionuclides not intended to be processed, provided activity concentration does not exceed 10 times values in §173.436.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and contamination thresholds (§173.403 — contamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines contamination and thresholds: contamination presence defined in Bq/cm2 for beta/gamma and alpha emitters; distinguishes fixed and non-fixed contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contamination exists in two phases: fixed radioactive contamination = cannot be removed during normal conditions of transport; non-fixed = can be removed. Thresholds: >0.4 Bq/cm2 for beta/gamma and low toxicity alpha emitters; >0.04 Bq/cm2 for all other alpha emitters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticality Safety Index (CSI) definition and calculation (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: CSI is a number (rounded up to next tenth) used to control accumulation of fissile packages; determined per 10 CFR 71.22, 71.23, 71.59; CSI for overpack/freight container/consignment is arithmetic sum of CSIs of contained fissile packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CSI for controlling accumulation in transport; follow referenced 10 CFR instructions for package CSI determination; sum CSIs for aggregates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive use shipment definition and consignor responsibilities (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive use = sole use of a conveyance by a single consignor where all loading/unloading are directed by consignor/consignee; consignor and carrier must ensure loading/unloading by personnel with radiological training and provide written instructions including vehicle survey requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consignor must provide specific written instructions for maintaining exclusive use controls (including vehicle survey requirement §173.443(c)), and include these with shipping paper info provided to the carrier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highway route controlled quantity (HRCQ) thresholds (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines HRCQ as quantity within a single package exceeding specified multiples of A1/A2 or absolute TBq limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HRCQ if exceeding: (1) 3,000 × A1 for special form radionuclides; (2) 3,000 × A2 for normal form radionuclides; or (3) 1,000 TBq (27,000 Ci), whichever is least.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited quantity of Class 7 definition (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited quantity means quantity not exceeding package limits in §173.425 and conforming with requirements in §173.421.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use §173.425 package limits and §173.421 requirements to determine limited quantity qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low Specific Activity (LSA) material categories and criteria (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: LSA materials are Class 7 materials with limited specific activity and are categorized as LSA-I, LSA-II, or LSA-III with distinct descriptions/limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSA-I examples: uranium/thorium ores intended for processing; solid unirradiated natural or depleted uranium or natural thorium; other non-fissile material with unlimited A2; other material with estimated average specific activity ≤30× values in §173.436 or Table 10B default values. LSA-II: water with tritium up to 0.8 TBq/L or other material with specified average specific activity limits (10^-4 A2/g for solids/gases, 10^-5 A2/g for liquids). LSA-III: solids (e.g., consolidated wastes, activated materials) meeting §173.468, relatively insoluble conditions limiting leaching to ≤0.1 A2 in 7 days, and estimated average specific activity ≤2×10^-3 A2/g (excluding shielding). Shielding not counted in estimating average specific activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freight container and small freight container definitions (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freight container defined by reusable container volume ≥1.81 m3 (64 ft3); small freight container defined by one outer dimension <1.5 m or internal volume ≤3.0 m3 (106 ft3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large freight containers are all others; definitions used in packaging and transport rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fissile material definition (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fissile material means plutonium-239, plutonium-241, uranium-233, uranium-235, or any combination; excludes certain unirradiated and reactor-irradiated uranium forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term does not apply to material containing fissile nuclides that are unirradiated natural uranium or unirradiated depleted uranium, or natural/depleted uranium irradiated only in thermal reactors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Package type definitions (excepted, industrial IP, Type A, Type B, Type B(U)/B(M)) (§173.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines package classes: excepted package, industrial package (IP-1/IP-2/IP-3), Type A (A1/A2 limits, tests per §173.465/173.466, no Competent Authority approval), Type B (designed for >A1/A2 quantities and subjected to normal/hypothetical accident tests per 10 CFR part 71), with Type B(U) unilateral approval and Type B(M) multilateral approval distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial package requirements in §§173.410-173.411; Type A requirements in §§173.410 and 173.412; Type B must meet 10 CFR part 71 test conditions. Type B(U) = unilateral approval for international shipments; Type B(M) = multilateral approval for international shipments and may require approval of shipment conditions.
